question: How many Bachelor or Master programmes can I apply for?
gold_answer_brief: An applicant can apply for a maximum of three programmes.

question: Does the University offer a spring or summer intake for Bachelor and Master programmes?
gold_answer_brief: No. Bachelor and Master programmes have one annual intake in September.

question: Can I modify or delete an application after I create it?
gold_answer_brief: No. Once an application has been created it cannot be modified or deleted.

question: Which file formats can I upload for an application and what is the maximum size per document?
gold_answer_brief: Documents must be uploaded as PDF JPG or PNG files with a maximum size of 5 MB per document.

question: Which documents are generally required for a Master's application?
gold_answer_brief: Typical documents include identification a university degree certificate Bachelor transcripts health-insurance proof and proof for all teaching languages. Some programmes request additional material.

question: Do applicants need to prove competence in every teaching language listed for their chosen programme?
gold_answer_brief: Yes. Applicants must prove the required competence in all listed teaching languages unless the programme page states otherwise.
notes: Gold labels corrected after official-source audit: the same language-competence rule appears on the main Bachelor/Master admissions page, Admission Criteria page and Proof of Language Skills page.

question: Can I be admitted in the current application cycle if I do not meet the required language level by the deadline?
gold_answer_brief: No. Applicants who do not meet the required level for all teaching languages before the deadline are not eligible in that application cycle.

question: What must a third-country applicant do about a foreign secondary-school diploma before applying for a Bachelor programme?
gold_answer_brief: The applicant must request recognition of the diploma's equivalence and submit the equivalence document by the applicable application deadline.

question: Is there a process for having prior studies or professional experience recognised?
gold_answer_brief: Yes. The University provides a recognition-of-prior-experience procedure for candidates whose prior learning may justify admission or exemptions.

question: What are the three faculties of the University of Luxembourg?
gold_answer_brief: The three faculties are FSTM FDEF and FHSE.

question: Where can I compare the University's Bachelor and Master study programmes?
gold_answer_brief: The Study Programme Overview is the central source for browsing Bachelor and Master programmes.

question: Which faculty offers the Bachelor in Computer Science?
gold_answer_brief: The Bachelor in Computer Science is offered by FSTM.

question: What are the duration ECTS total and teaching language of the Bachelor in Computer Science?
gold_answer_brief: The programme has 180 ECTS lasts three years or six semesters and is taught in English.

question: How long is the Master in Data Science and how many ECTS does it contain?
gold_answer_brief: The Master in Data Science contains 120 ECTS and lasts two years or four semesters.

question: Can the Master in Data Science be followed with part-time student status?
gold_answer_brief: Yes. The programme is full-time but part-time student status is allowed.

question: What are the duration ECTS total and teaching language of the Master in Finance and Economics?
gold_answer_brief: The programme has 120 ECTS lasts two years or four semesters and is taught in English.

question: What are the duration ECTS total and teaching language of the Master in Social Sciences and Educational Sciences?
gold_answer_brief: The programme has 120 ECTS lasts two years or four semesters and is taught in English.

question: Which faculty offers the Bachelor en Droit?
gold_answer_brief: The Bachelor en Droit is offered by FDEF.

question: Which faculty offers the Bachelor en Sciences de l'éducation?
gold_answer_brief: The Bachelor en Sciences de l'éducation is offered by FHSE.

question: Do Bachelor and Master students have to re-enrol every semester?
gold_answer_brief: Yes. Students must re-enrol in their programme each semester and in their study track where applicable.

question: Why might a student's re-enrolment not be validated?
gold_answer_brief: Re-enrolment may be refused because compulsory documents are missing the maximum study duration was exceeded or study progression is insufficient.

question: Should a returning student create a new student ID number for re-enrolment?
gold_answer_brief: No. The original student ID number is valid for life and must be reused.

question: What payment methods are available for enrolment or re-enrolment fees?
gold_answer_brief: Fees can be paid by bank transfer online through the admission portal or by card in person at the Admission Office.

question: Can enrolment or re-enrolment fees be refunded after payment?
gold_answer_brief: No. Enrolment and re-enrolment fees are not refundable after payment.

question: When is a student considered fully enrolled?
gold_answer_brief: A student is fully enrolled only after tuition fees and any applicable health-insurance fees have been paid in full.

question: Which three decisions are covered by the annual study-progression assessment?
gold_answer_brief: The decision covers re-enrolment advancement to the next study year and course enrolment.

question: What does conditional progression mean for a student who earned between 50 and 70 percent of the required credits?
gold_answer_brief: The student advances when re-enrolling but course enrolments require approval from the Study Programme Director.

question: What happens to a first-year student whose progression is below 50 percent of the credit requirement?
gold_answer_brief: The progression is unsatisfactory and the first-year student is excluded from the programme and cannot re-enrol in the same programme.

question: Can using content generated or modified by a chatbot count as academic fraud?
gold_answer_brief: Yes. Using chatbot or AI-generated or modified content can constitute fraud when it is unauthorised.

question: What kinds of study-related decisions can a student or applicant appeal?
gold_answer_brief: Appealable decisions include admission recognition of prior experience assessment progression re-enrolment exclusion graduation leave extenuating circumstances and reasonable accommodation.

question: Can I appeal a grade only because I think the marker should have awarded a higher mark?
gold_answer_brief: No. Academic judgement alone cannot be appealed; evidence of procedural error lack of due diligence or impaired or biased judgement is needed.

question: What types of special arrangements are available to Bachelor and Master students?
gold_answer_brief: The source covers reasonable adjustments leaves of absence exemptions from study requirements and extenuating circumstances.

question: Which official document contains the University's general study rules for Bachelor and Master students?
gold_answer_brief: The general rules are contained in the University's Study Regulations.
notes: Gold labels corrected after official-source audit: the Official Documents page and the linked Study Regulations PDF both answer this document-identification question.

question: Which official document contains programme-specific regulatory provisions for Bachelor programmes for 2026-2027?
gold_answer_brief: The Bachelor Annex contains the programme-specific Bachelor provisions for 2026-2027.

question: Does the University guarantee accommodation and can I choose a specific residence?
gold_answer_brief: No. Accommodation is subject to availability and applicants cannot choose a specific residence or location.
